result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns `response` from `fetch(...)`), while the Hubspot caller assigns it as `HubspotToken` and computes expiry from `.expires_in` and persists derived keys, with no parseRefreshTokenResponse usage in hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts. So when sharing is enabled the hubspot code consumes a Response object lacking token fields, producing NaN expiry and a bad persisted credential.

judged_text: With sharing enabled the value assigned to hubspotRefreshToken is a raw fetch Response rather than a HubspotToken, and Response objects have no refresh_token, expires_in or access_token properties. Hubspot token refresh computes expiry_date from an undefined expires_in (NaN) and persists a Response-derived object as the credential key, bricking the Hubspot integration for sharing-enabled deployments.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `hubspotRefreshToken` is now assigned the return value of `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When sharing is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` object, not parsed JSON. Hubspot’s refresh logic expects a `HubspotToken` object (e.g., `expires_in`, `access_token`, etc.) from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`, so under sharing-enabled deployments it will operate on a `Response` without those properties, leading to undefined/NaN expiry calculations and incorrect credential persistence.
